What We Do

Full-Service Hospitalist Revenue Cycle Management

Hospitalist billing requires high-volume inpatient E/M coding, critical care time aggregation, discharge day management, and co-attending coordination across large patient panels. PMEX reviews clinical documentation and codes every encounter before submission.

Admission E/M Coding

Initial hospital care (99221 to 99223) coded at correct complexity from the admission note.

Subsequent Visit Coding

Daily inpatient E/M (99231 to 99233) coded from the daily progress note per MDM.

Critical Care Billing

99291 and 99292 coded from documented critical care time across all chart entries.

Discharge Day Billing

99238 and 99239 applied correctly based on total discharge day time documented.

Observation Coding

Observation admission and discharge codes applied per patient status at each transition.

Co-Attending Coordination

Split/shared visit rules applied when attending and APP share care on the same day.

Sound Familiar?

Common Hospitalist Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Every inpatient visit defaulted to level 2 (99232) regardless of MDM complexity.

PMEX codes subsequent visits from the daily progress note MDM, capturing level 3 when the complexity supports it.

Critical care time not aggregated across multiple chart entries, missing 99292 add-on units.

PMEX aggregates all critical care documentation for the calendar day and bills 99292 when total time exceeds 74 minutes.

Discharge day time not documented, preventing 99239 (greater than 30 minutes) from being billed.

PMEX confirms discharge day time is documented before selecting 99238 or 99239 on every discharge encounter.

Split/shared visit between attending and APP not documented correctly, losing the higher attending rate.

PMEX applies 2023 CMS split/shared rules and confirms the substantive portion is documented by the billing provider.

Observation to inpatient conversion not coded, leaving the admission E/M uncaptured.

PMEX tracks status changes from observation to inpatient and codes the correct admission E/M on the conversion date.

Consultations billed as subsequent visits, missing the initial consultation revenue.

PMEX applies the correct inpatient consultation framework per payer, including modifier use where required.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Hospitalist Billing

Hospitalist groups lose 14 to 22 percent of revenue to E/M level defaults, critical care time errors, and split/shared documentation failures.

PATTERN 01

Subsequent Visit Defaulted to Level 2 on Every Patient

All subsequent inpatient visits submitted as 99232 regardless of clinical complexity. High-complexity patients with multiple active problems, extensive data review, and high-risk decisions qualify for 99233 ($180 vs. $125). $55 per visit on qualifying encounters.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX codes every subsequent visit from the progress note MDM, identifying the number of problems addressed, data reviewed, and risk level. Level 3 is coded when the documentation supports it.

PATTERN 02

Critical Care Billed Without Aggregating Time Across the Day

Hospitalist documents critical care at 7 AM (25 minutes) and 2 PM (30 minutes) for a total of 55 minutes. Only 99291 submitted. 99292 not billed. 55 minutes is below the add-on threshold (74 minutes). However, a third entry at 6 PM (22 minutes) brings total to 77 minutes. That entry was not reviewed. $120 missed.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews all chart entries for the calendar day before coding critical care, aggregating time across morning rounds, afternoon reassessments, and evening notes to confirm the total documented critical care time.

PATTERN 03

Discharge Day Time Not Documented, 99239 Not Billed

Physician spends 45 minutes on discharge activities. Does not document the time spent. 99238 (30 minutes or less) submitted. 99239 (more than 30 minutes, $180 vs. $120) could not be billed without time documentation. $60 per discharge lost.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews discharge notes for time documentation before selecting 99238 or 99239. When time is absent, the coding team flags the note for physician addendum before the claim is submitted.

Questions

Hospitalist Billing Questions Answered

Using 2021 AMA Medical Decision-Making criteria. Level 1 (99231): straightforward MDM. Level 2 (99232): low to moderate MDM. Level 3 (99233): moderate to high MDM with multiple active problems, data review, and high-risk decisions.

Per CMS, critical care time is cumulative for the calendar day. We aggregate all documented critical care time across chart entries before billing 99291 and 99292.

99238 (30 minutes or less) and 99239 (more than 30 minutes) are based on total discharge day time. Time must be documented. We flag notes without time documentation for addendum before billing.

Under 2023 CMS rules, the billing provider is the one who performs the substantive portion of the visit. We apply the correct billing provider NPI based on who performed the substantive portion per the documented chart.

Yes. We track observation admission codes, inpatient conversion codes, and discharge codes through every patient status transition during the hospital stay.
